test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

She said to me, "Would you like some coffee?"

options.text: She asked that I would like some coffee.
She asked me if I would like some coffee.
She asked me would I like some coffee.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She asked me if I would like some coffee.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Would you like some coffee" becomes "if I would like some coffee"**
 
 
• The question form is converted into a statement by using "if."
 
• The pronoun "you" is changed to "I" to match indirect speech.
 
• The modal verb "would" remains unchanged as it is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: "said to me"
 
• Converted to: "asked me" to reflect the nature of the question.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted into an indirect statement without quotation marks.
 
• The reporting verb is followed by the conjunction "if."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She asked me if I would like some coffee.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She asked that I would like some coffee." 

 
 
• Incorrect because "that" is not used in indirect questions.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She asked me would I like some coffee." 
 
 
• Incorrect word order for indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She offered me some coffee." 
 
 
• Changes the intent from a question to an offer, altering the meaning.
